subject: Use stamped fast-sword state when translating PassDoor
description: The completed-sweep actor.animation cluster representative, schema-14 SuN1Sh1nE Profile_004 Savegame_001 replay-001, first diverged after frame 1600 for selected PC 252 (Robin): Original installed animation 304 (RHNONANIMATION_RUNNING_WITH_SWORD) while Rust installed animation 10 (RHANIMATION_RUNNING_UPRIGHT). Robin had just completed a RunningWithSword MoveOk at building door 99; its following direct PassDoor element was stamped Upright/MovingFastSword with FAST. Original RHElementActorHuman::DetermineMovementAnimation switches on the movement element's GetPostureAfterTransition/GetActionStateAfterTransition values, and _ANY_SWORD_ACTIONSTATE_ explicitly includes RHACTIONSTATE_MOVING_FAST_SWORD, so the authored RunningUpright action is rewritten to RunningWithSword before TranslatePassDoorBuilding constructs its rail orders. Rust's door builder instead read the actor's live state through a hand-written sword category that omitted MovingFastSword and invented Menacing membership, producing an ordinary running rail and changing the live action state from MovingFastSword to MovingFast. PassDoor translation now threads the element-stamped posture and action state into its builder, uses the canonical is_sword/is_shield categories (with the shield override restricted to PCs as in Original), and uses the stamped posture for lift movement translation. A focused direct-building regression deliberately gives the PC a live Waiting state but stamps the PassDoor Upright/MovingFastSword with FAST, then requires both the movement element's rewritten root action and its first rail order to be RunningWithSword. cargo test -p robin_engine direct_pc_pass_uses_stamped_moving_fast_sword_state passes 1/1, cargo fmt is clean, and git diff --check is clean. On the optimized Task145 parity runner target/parity/parity/examples/original_parity_replay dated 2026-08-08 11:12:34.709671703 +0200, the SuN representative and both task-36 schema-14 controls, Cyrdach Profile_156 Savegame_001 replay-009 and Nescafe Profile_001 Savegame_001 replay-009, match every recorded frame through exact EOF.
